translations.text: And these are the words of the book which Baruch, son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, son of Zedekiah, son of Hasadiah, son of Hilkiah, wrote in Babylon,
in the fourth year, in the seventh month, at the time when the Chaldeans took Jerusalem and burned it with fire.
And Baruch read the words of this book aloud in the hearing of Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and in the hearing of all the people who had come to the book,

and in the hearing of the mighty men and the king's sons, and in the hearing of the elders, and in the hearing of all the people, from the least to the greatest: all who lived in Babylon by the river Sud.
And they wept and fasted and prayed before the Lord;
and they collected silver, as much as each person could give,
and sent it to Jerusalem, to Jehoiakim the priest, son of Hilkiah, son of Shallum, and to the other priests, and to all the people who were found with them in Jerusalem,

at the time when he took the vessels of the house of the Lord, which had been carried away from the temple, to return them to the land of Judah, on the tenth of Sivan. These were the silver vessels which Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, had made

after Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took captives, when he carried Jeconiah away from Jerusalem as a captive, together with his princes, the offerers, the craftsmen, the rich, and the people of the land, and brought them to Babylon.
And they said: “Behold, we have sent you silver. With the silver, buy your offerings for sins, and incense, and prepare grain offerings (manaa), and offer them on the altar of the Lord our God.
And pray for the life of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and for the life of Belshazzar his son, so that their days on earth may be like the days of heaven,

and so that the Lord may give us strength and give light to our eyes, so that we may live under the shade of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and under the shade of Belshazzar his son, and serve them for many days, and find favour in their sight.
And pray for us to the Lord our God, because we have sinned against the Lord our God, and the anger of the Lord and his wrath have not turned away from us to this very day.
And read this book which we have sent you, as a confession in the house of the Lord on the feast day and on the days of the appointed seasons.
And say: Righteousness belongs to the Lord our God, but shame belongs to your faces, as it does this day to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem,
and to our kings, and our princes, and our priests, and our prophets, and our fathers, before the Lord.
For we have been disobedient to him,
and we did not listen to the voice of the Lord our God, to walk in the commandments of the Lord which he set before us.
For from the day when he brought our fathers out of the land of Egypt until this very day, we have been disobedient to the Lord our God, and we turned away so that we would not listen to him,

and evil has overtaken us, along with the curse which the Lord gave to his servant Moses on the day he brought our fathers out of Egypt to give us a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is this day.
And we did not listen to the voice of the Lord our God in any of the words of the prophets whom he sent to us;
And each of us went after the thoughts of his own evil heart, to serve foreign gods and to do evil before the eyes of the Lord our God.
And the Lord fulfilled his word, which he spoke against us, against our judges who judged Israel, against our kings, against our princes, and against the men of Israel and of Judah,
to bring upon us great evil, such as has never happened anywhere under heaven, as he did in Jerusalem, as it is written in the law of Moses,
that we should eat, one man the flesh of his son and another the flesh of his daughter.
And he gave them over to be despised by all the kingdoms around us, to be a reproach and a desolation among all the peoples around us, where the Lord scattered them.
And they were brought low and not raised high, because we sinned against the Lord our God by not listening to his voice.
Righteousness belongs to the Lord our God, but to us and to our fathers belongs shame of face, as it is this day.
All the evils that the Lord spoke concerning us have come upon us,
and we did not entreat the face of the Lord, so that each of us would turn from the thoughts of his evil heart.
And the Lord kept watch to bring evils upon us, for the Lord is righteous in all his works which he commanded us;
and we did not listen to his voice, to walk in the commandments of the Lord which he set before our face.
And now, O Lord God of Israel, who brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a strong hand, with signs, with great power and with a high arm, and made a name for yourself, as it is this day:
we have sinned, we have become ungodly, we have acted lawlessly, O Lord our God, against all your ordinances.
Turn your anger away from us, for we are left few out of many among the nations where you scattered us.
Hear, O Lord, our prayer and our supplication, and deliver us for your own sake, and give us favor in the sight of those who carried us away captive,
so that all the earth may know that you are the Lord our God, and that your name is called upon Israel and upon his people.
O Lord, look down from your holy temple and consider us; incline your ear, O Lord, and hear us;
open your eyes, O Lord, and see: it is not the dead who are in Hades, whose spirits have been taken [?] from their inner parts, who will give glory and justice to the Lord.
But the soul that grieves [?] over the greatness of its distress, that goes about bowed down [?] and weak, with failing eyes, and the hungry soul will give you glory and justice, O Lord.
For it is not because of the righteous deeds of our fathers and our kings that we lay our plea for mercy before your face, O Lord our God;
for you have brought your anger and your wrath upon us, as you spoke by the hand of your servants the prophets, saying:
"Thus said the Lord: Bend your shoulders and serve the king of Babylon, and dwell in the land which I gave to your fathers.
But if you do not listen to the voice of the Lord and serve the king of Babylon,

I will make the voice of mirth and the voice of joy, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, cease from the cities of Judah and from around Jerusalem, and the whole land will become a desolation without inhabitants."

But we did not listen to your voice and serve the king of Babylon. So you carried out the words you spoke through your servants the prophets: that the bones of our kings and the bones of our fathers would be taken out of their resting places.
And now they lie scattered, exposed to the heat of the day and the frost of the night. For they died in great suffering, by famine, by the sword and in captivity.
And you made the house that was called by your name a ruin, as it is today, because of the wickedness of the house of Israel and the house of Judah.
Yet you have dealt with us, O Lord my God, with all your gentleness and with your great mercy,
as you said through your servant Moses on the day you commanded him to write your law before the children of Israel. You said:
"If you do not listen to my voice, then surely this great and numerous multitude [?] will be turned back far away among the nations, where I will scatter them.
For I know that they will not listen to me, because they are a stiff-necked people. But in the land of their captivity they will turn back in their hearts,
and they will understand that I am the Lord their God. I will give them an understanding heart and obedient ears,
and they will praise me in the land of their captivity and remember my name.
They will turn away from their stiff-neckedness and from their wicked deeds, because they will remember the way of their fathers, who sinned before the Lord.

And I will bring them back to the land that I promised on oath to their fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. They will take possession of it, and I will make them many, and they will not be made few again.
I will make an everlasting covenant with them, so that I will be their God and they will be my people. And I will never again remove my people Israel from the land that I have given them."
O Lord Almighty, God of Israel, a soul in distress and a weary spirit cries out to you.
Hear, O Lord, and have mercy, for you are a merciful God. Have mercy on us, for we have sinned before you.
For you endure forever, but we are perishing forever.

O Lord Almighty, God of Israel, hear the voice of the dead of Israel and of the children of those who sinned before you. They did not listen to the voice of the Lord their God, and so evil has come upon us.
Do not remember the wrongdoing of our fathers. Instead, remember your hand and your name at this time.
For you are the Lord our God, and we will praise you, O Lord.

For this reason you have put the fear of you into our hearts, so that we would call on your name. And we will praise you in our captivity, because we have put away from our hearts all the wrongdoing of our fathers, who sinned before you.

See, we are in our captivity today, where you have scattered us. We have become an object of scorn and a curse, and we are made to pay for all the wrongdoing of our fathers, who turned away from the Lord our God.
Hear the commandments of life, O Israel. Listen closely, to learn wisdom.
Why is it, Israel, that you are in the land of your enemies, that you have [grown old?] in a foreign land, and that you are defiled along with the dead,
and counted among those who are in hell?
You have abandoned the fountain of wisdom.
If you had walked in the way of God, you would have lived in peace forever.
Ask where wisdom is, where strength is, where understanding is, so that you may know at the same time where length of days and life are, where the light of the eyes and peace are.
Who has found her place, and who has entered into her treasuries?
Where are the rulers of the nations, and those who had dominion over the beasts of the earth,
and who scorned the birds of heaven, and who stored up silver and gold, in which people trusted, and there is no end to their acquiring?
They carved silver and were anxious over it, and there is no searching out of their works.
They perished and went down to hell, and other young men rose up in their place.
They saw the light and dwelt upon the earth, but they did not know the way of knowledge,
nor did they understand her paths, nor did they receive her; their children went far from their way.
She was not heard of in Canaan, nor was she seen in Teman,

nor among the sons of Hagar who seek out understanding on the earth, the princes of Merran and of Teman, and the [?] and the seekers of knowledge; but they did not understand the way of wisdom, nor did they remember her paths.
O Israel, how great is the house of God, and how long is the place of his dwelling!
It is great and has no end; it is high and beyond measure.
There the giants were born, the renowned, who were great from the beginning, skilled in war.
God did not choose these, nor did he give them the way of knowledge;
and they perished because they had no understanding; they perished through their folly.
Who has gone up into heaven and taken hold of her, and brought her down from the clouds?
Who has crossed over the sea and found her, and brought her back for choice gold?
There is no one who knows her way, nor anyone who understands her paths,
but he who knows all things knows her; he searched her out by his understanding, he who prepared the earth for all time and filled it with four-footed creatures,
he who sends out the light and it goes; he called it, and it answered him with trembling.
And the stars shone in their seasons and rejoiced.
He called them, and they said, "Here we are"; they shone with joy for their Creator.
This is our God; no other can be compared with him.
He revealed the whole way of knowledge and gave it to Jacob his servant and to Israel his beloved.
After this she appeared on earth and lived among people.
This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endures forever. All who receive it will live, and those who abandon it will perish.
Turn, Jacob, and keep it, and walk before the brightness of its light.
Do not give your glory to another, or your good things to a foreign nation.
Blessed are we, Israel, for the will of God has been made known to us.
Do not be afraid, my people, redeemed Israel.
You were sold among the nations, but not to be destroyed. You were handed over to your enemies because you angered God.
For you angered your Creator by the [?] of demons and not of God.
You forgot the eternal God who raised you, and you grieved Jerusalem, who nursed you.
For she saw the wrath from God that had come upon you, and she said: "Listen, you who live near Zion, for God has sent everlasting mourning upon me.
For I have seen the captivity of my sons and my daughters, which the Everlasting brought upon them.
For I raised them with joy, and I sent them away with weeping and mourning.
Let no one give a foot [?] to me, a widow cast down by many. I have been made desolate because of the sins of my children, for they turned away from the law of God.
They did not understand his ordinances, nor did they walk in the ways of God's commandments, nor did they stand in the paths of instruction in the truth of his righteousness.
Come, you who live near Zion, and remember the captivity of my sons and my daughters, which the Everlasting brought upon them.
For he brought against them a nation from far away, a shameless nation with a foreign language. They had no respect for the old, and they had no pity on the child.
They carried off the widow's beloved ones, and they left me alone as a widow, without my daughters.
But how can I help you?
The one who brought this evil on you is the one who will rescue you from the hands of your enemies.
Go, children, go, for I am left desolate.
I have taken off the robe of peace and put on the sackcloth of my supplication, and I will cry out to the Everlasting all my days.
Do not be afraid, children. Cry out to God, and he will rescue you from the power of your enemies' hands.
For I hope in the Everlasting for your rescue. Joy has come to me from the Holy One because of the mercy toward you that will soon come from the Everlasting, our Savior.
For I sent you out with mourning and weeping, but God will give you back to me with joy and gladness forever.
For just as those who live near Zion have now seen your captivity, so they will soon see your rescue from your God. It will come to you with great glory and with the splendor of the Everlasting.
Children, endure patiently the wrath that has come upon you from God. Your enemy has persecuted you, but you will soon see his destruction, and you will set your foot on his neck.
My delicate ones walked rough roads; they were carried off like a flock seized by enemies.
Do not be afraid, children, and cry out to God, for you will be remembered by him who brought this upon you.
For just as your heart was set on straying from God, turn back ten times over to seek him.
For he who brought evil upon you will bring you everlasting joy along with your deliverance.
Do not be afraid, Jerusalem; he who gave you your name comforts you.
Wretched are those who did you evil and who rejoiced at your fall;
wretched are those cities that your children served as slaves; wretched is she who received your sons.
For just as she rejoiced at your fall and was glad at your ruin, so she will grieve over her own desolation.
And I will take away from her the joy of her great multitude of people, and her gladness will turn into mourning.
For fire will come upon her from the Everlasting for many days, and demons will dwell in her for a very long time.
Look toward the east, Jerusalem, and see the joy that is coming to you from God.
Behold, your children whom you sent away are coming; they are coming gathered together from the east to the west at the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of God.
Take off, Jerusalem, the garment of your mourning and of your affliction, and put on forever the beauty of the glory that comes from God.
Put on the cloak of the righteousness that comes from God, and set on your head the headdress [?] of everlasting glory.
For God will show your splendor to every end of the heavens,
for God will call you by your name forever: "Peace of Righteousness and Glory of Hope in God."

Arise, Jerusalem, stand upon the height, and look toward the east, and see your children gathered from the setting of the sun to the east; at the word of the Holy One they rejoice that God has remembered them.
For they went out from you [?] (on foot?), led away by enemies, but God has brought them back to you, exalted in glory like royal thrones.
For God has commanded that every high mountain and the everlasting hills be made low, and that the valleys be filled up to make the ground level, so that Israel may walk safely in the glory of God.
For even the woods and every fragrant tree have given shade to Israel at God's command;
for God will lead Israel with joy in the light of his glory, together with his mercy and his righteousness.
